I'm reading these before I write anything. SKILL.md tells me to read the discovery and Claude Code references before drafting frontmatter and body, and the bulletproofing and persuasion references before wording the counters. I also want the exact rationalizations from your baseline file in front of me, not from memory.

This is a discipline failure: the agents know better and skip the step under pressure. So I plan to use the prohibition form: a clear rule, a rationalization table built from the verbatim baseline quotes ("staging is disposable", "only additive", "takes too long"), and a red-flags list. The description will contain triggering conditions only ("Use when applying a database migration to any environment, including staging"), with no workflow summary, so agents can't take the description as a shortcut and skip the body.

After the reads I'll write `skills/migration-dry-run/SKILL.md` and send it for your review. Then I'll re-run the same four scenarios with the skill present. The RED baseline is done, but GREEN still needs that run before the skill counts as verified.
